descriptions.collection_id: Selected collection label: the file or query the record came from. Together with source_record_id identifies this record; joins fec_collections.collection_id and, for the election cycle, fec_collection_cycles.collection_id.

descriptions.source_record_id: Provider source-record identity, native API identity, bulk file key or byte-evidenced positional/agency-report observation ID, scoped to collection_id.
descriptions.committee_id: Committee ID as the source reports it (bulk CMTE_ID or the API's committee_id). In transaction files this is the committee that filed the report, not necessarily the one that received the money: a PAC's contribution to a candidate is filed under the PAC's ID, with the recipient in metadata_json OTHER_ID and CAND_ID, and TRANSACTION_TP says which way the money moved. To find money a committee received from other committees, also search OTHER_ID: in the 2025-2026 file a candidate committee's own filings list no direct PAC contributions, so they appear only under each PAC's committee_id, with the candidate in OTHER_ID and CAND_ID (TRANSACTION_TP 24K). May join fec_committees.committee_id. Blanks remain blank; no identifier is inferred from a name or another entity's ID.
descriptions.candidate_id: Literal candidate identifier reported by API metadata or a verified named bulk field such as CAND_ID. Blanks and aggregate codes remain literal; an ID-shaped aggregate value does not establish a person. Names are not converted to identifiers.
descriptions.filing_id: Source-reported sub_id of a filing metadata row when present; not an inferred original-file number. Amendment/current-record meaning remains in native metadata.
descriptions.legal_doc_id: Source-reported legal document identifier when present, retained in its original source scope.
descriptions.audit_case_id: Source-reported audit case identifier when present.
descriptions.source_sha256: Digest pinning the source bytes from which the provider observed this record.
descriptions.source_url: Recorded source URL associated with the observation; this is evidence provenance, not a live availability check.
descriptions.observed_at: Provider observation time when available, distinct from dates reported inside the source record.
descriptions.source_locator_json: JSON source coordinates identifying the original response field, record, file or ZIP member and byte span when supplied. Optional field_mapping pins the selected source header or HTML field dictionary; complete dictionary cells appear in the parent collection's tableFieldDefinitions.
descriptions.metadata_json: Retained metadata whose shape depends on the source/profile, not a uniformly unwrapped case object. Inspect `json_keys(metadata_json)` first. The observed `api-record-observation` wrapper keeps the case under `metadata`: for MUR 8074, use `json_extract(metadata_json, '$.metadata.dispositions')`, not `$.dispositions`; `json_keys(metadata_json, '$.metadata')` shows the case fields. Other native legal records can be unwrapped, while bulk records carry positional or verified named fields and PostgreSQL records expose `named_fields`. Do not apply this wrapper path to every family. Prefer `fec_legal_matters`, `fec_legal_events`, `fec_legal_parties` and `fec_legal_documents` for typed legal queries. Memo and attribution fields still require source-specific inclusion rules; raw mapping does not establish a safe total. Header/blank rows retain positional metadata; `source_record_json` retains the full provider source record.
descriptions.assets_json: JSON representation of provider asset references and evidence; an asset reference alone does not establish that its body was downloaded.
descriptions.embedded_bodies_json: JSON representation of provider-embedded body values, retaining their supplied scope.
descriptions.source_record_json: Complete provider source-record serialization, preserving identity, native metadata, assets, bodies and evidence.
